sparcs_validation.validation_strategy: GroupKFold(n_splits=5, groups=Facility ID) ensuring zero facility leakage across train and test folds.
sparcs_validation.honest_verdict: performance is at baseline level; band accuracy is dominated by the 89% short-stay class

direct_cross_dataset_transfer.root_cause: Extreme distributional base rate shift: In SPARCS, 89.1% of stays are <= 10 days (Band 0), whereas in Kaggle Healthcare Analytics II, Band 0 comprises only 7.4% of admissions. A model trained on Kaggle expects a 32-day average stay and systematically overpredicts stay lengths when applied to a standard US discharge population, leading to near-zero accuracy.

sparcs_validation.macro_f1_averaging_note: All macro-F1 scores strictly average across all 11 syllabus classes (labels 0..10). Earlier draft reported ~0.1044 (majority) and ~0.1228 (ANN) because scikit-learn without explicit class labels averaged only over the 9 active classes present in test folds (0.9423 / 9 = 0.1047 vs 0.9423 / 11 = 0.0856).

simulator.calibration_scope_note: The simulator is calibrated to state-level HHS aggregates and Little's Law dynamics; it is not validated against real hospital internal patient records.
simulator.data_stay_origin_note: Inpatient stay lengths come from empirical Kaggle patient profiles with mean stay of approximately 32.3 days (32.26 days).
simulator.baseline_vs_scenario_occupancy_explanati: In the 3-year baseline simulation, peak occupancy reaches 95.0% (0.9500 max occupancy) with 0 capacity shortfall days, as baseline Poisson arrivals (2.715/day) combined with mild winter seasonality (1.12x) remain within the 120-bed buffer. Conversely, under the 60-day 1.35x flu surge stress test, admission rates jump by +35% to 3.67/day, which severely overwhelms the 120-bed buffer and drives peak patient demand to 113.3% (136 total patient demand = 120 licensed beds + 16 overflow demand) across 28 shortfall days.

calibration_study.class_weighted_ann_note: scikit-learn MLPClassifier has no 'class_weight' parameter and its .fit() method does not accept 'sample_weight'. An earlier run attempted compute_sample_weight but because MLPClassifier does not consume weights, it produced output identical to unweighted training (log-loss 1.5237). The invalid duplicate row has been removed. True probability calibration is achieved via CalibratedClassifierCV (isotonic / sigmoid) and decision threshold optimization rather than sample weighting.

majority_baselines.11_band_brier_verdict: Better than both uniform guessing (0.909) and majority-class assignment (1.450), though modest in absolute terms.

step3_feature_selection_and_ablations.provenance_note: Earlier feature selection scores (macro-F1 ~0.16 to 0.22) were produced by a RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=40, max_depth=12) on 3-fold GroupKFold. The benchmarks below evaluate both Decision Tree and ANN across 5-fold GroupKFold.

step6_sparcs_censored_em.methodology: Interval-censored Gaussian mixture on log-scale with variance floor sigma >= 0.20
step6_sparcs_censored_em.selection_rationale: k=6 selected as it strictly minimizes BIC (9,455,310.4) and maximizes held-out log-likelihood (-1,181,904.9) across all tested models (k=2..6). All components sit at valid empirical dispersions (sigma in [0.201, 0.920], max 0.92) without spike collapse.
step6_sparcs_censored_em.simulator_tail_usage: For Kaggle's '>100 days' band (Band 10), src/simulator.py lines 103-108 draws stays from a truncated log-normal distribution with mu=4.75, sigma=0.15 bounded between log(101) and log(150), yielding stays between 101 and 150 days.

facility_raw_cross_check.cross_check_note: Facility median bed capacity (109 beds) aligns with our 120-bed simulated hospital model. Disparity between unweighted facility mean (56.5%) and state-aggregated mean (74.5%) reflects rural critical-access standby capacity vs. urban tertiary hospital utilization.

step11_hmm_surge.trained_on_series: Rhode Island HHS state time series (70% chronological split, 1,057 days from 2020-01-01 to 2022-11-23)

model_selection.selection_rule: Lowest BIC and highest held-out log-likelihood on chronological 70/30 split
model_selection.bic_verdict: k=4 selected strictly by BIC (-9,466.6 vs -9,139.7 for k=3) and held-out log-likelihood (2,258.2 vs 2,223.4).

rules.conditions: Current occupancy >= 90% OR HMM State == 3 (Critical Surge) OR Next-day surge risk >= 50%
rules.protocol: CRITICAL SURGE PROTOCOL: Pause elective admissions, activate discharge lounge, open reserve overflow beds.

rules.conditions: Current occupancy in [85%, 90%) OR HMM State == 2 (Pre-Surge) OR Next-day surge risk in [20%, 50%)
rules.protocol: SURGE ALERT PROTOCOL: Notify on-call nursing teams, expedite discharge rounds, review step-down candidates.

rules.conditions: Current occupancy < 85% AND HMM State in {0, 1} AND Next-day surge risk < 20%
rules.protocol: NORMAL OPERATIONS: Standard patient intake and routine discharge rounds.

operational_verdict.verdict: no better than the 85% rule (different recall/false-alarm trade-off)
operational_verdict.recommendation: The HMM is no better than the 85% rule (different recall/false-alarm trade-off). In low-surge states (AZ, SC, WV), state-level surges are sudden and isolated with 0 advance warning across all methods. In high-surge states (RI), occupancy remains elevated, causing lead times to saturate the 14-day search cap. Therefore, the simple calibrated rule (>= 85% alert) is recommended for operational hospital triage, with HMM retained as an experimental regime decoder.

algorithms.decoding_algorithm: Viterbi algorithm (dynamic programming maximum a posteriori path estimation)

dataset_sources.simulated_hospital: 120-bed simulated facility, 60 walk-forward origins across years 2 and 3 (split into 30 calib / 30 test origins)
dataset_sources.real_hhs_aggregates: 480 walk-forward origins across 4 states (RI, AZ, SC, DE)

step12_forecast_evaluation.real_hhs_model_description: The real HHS benchmark model is a Mean-Reverting Autoregressive Filter: O_hat_{t+h} = rho^h * O_t + (1 - rho^h) * MA7_t, with persistence parameter rho = 0.95. It captures the empirical autocorrelation structure of aggregate health system capacity by smoothly transitioning from instantaneous 24-hour persistence toward the trailing 7-day moving average.
step12_forecast_evaluation.rho_tuning_note: rho = 0.95 was pre-specified a priori from typical 24-hour census autocorrelation decay (rho ~ 0.95, representing ~14-day half-life of inpatient stay decay). An exploratory grid sweep on an independent earlier training window (480 earlier chronological origins across RI, AZ, SC, DE) confirmed rho in [0.80, 0.95] achieves 1.82 to 1.98 pp overall MAE, with rho=0.95 providing superior Day 7 tracking (1.68 pp vs 1.86 pp for rho=0.80).

honest_verdict.pure_monte_carlo_model: does not beat baselines at any horizon for point MAE due to extreme 24h census autocorrelation
honest_verdict.blended_persistence_variant: reduces Day 1 point MAE from 3.19 pp to 2.03 pp (beating 7D MA and Seasonal-Naive), but remains behind 24h persistence (1.64 pp)
honest_verdict.surge_evaluation_limitation: Surge detection metrics rested on only 1 to 4 events per horizon; officially labeled 'too few events to judge (N < 20)'

step13_ward_summing.evaluation_cohort: 63,688 admissions across 18,403 held-out patients (GroupKFold test fold)
step13_ward_summing.ground_truth_note: Actual stay days are represented by band midpoints (5 to 110 days).
step13_ward_summing.clt_benchmark_clarification: The 1/sqrt(N) curve represents the single-patient empirical MAPE scaled by 1/sqrt(N) (e1 / sqrt(N)), serving as a reference benchmark for independent error decay rather than a mathematical theorem bound. Random patient sampling represents a theoretical best-case scenario with maximal diversity; same-department wards show slightly attenuated cancellation (e.g. 8.75% in Gynecology vs 8.51% in random at N=20) due to intra-service clinical similarity, but still achieve massive error reduction down to 5.28% - 5.74% at N=50.
step13_ward_summing.causality_disclaimer: All feature associations, decision-tree split rules, and clustering profiles represent statistical associations, not clinical causes.

gynecology_patient_count_audit.note: 49,999 is the exact count of admissions in the 20% GroupKFold test fold for Gynecology (from 16,834 unique patients), not an artificial cap. The full Kaggle dataset contains 249,486 Gynecology admissions across 83,951 unique patients.

kaggle_train_data.computation_method: Exact count from pandas read_csv on raw Data/train_data.csv using df['patientid'].nunique() and len(df).

kaggle_test_data.computation_method: Exact count from pandas read_csv on raw Data/test_data.csv; target Stay column is absent.

sparcs_2014.computation_method: Line count (minus header) and pandas non-null check across Length of Stay and Facility ID. Note: Earlier mention of 2,332,492 in text was an unverified load; true disk row count is 2,367,550.

hhs_state_timeseries.computation_method: Line count on CSV minus header; dropped 352 rows where inpatient_beds was null or <= 0.

hhs_facility_raw.computation_method: Exact line count on CSV minus header.

step4_target_definitions_verified.definition_reconciliation_note: The 3-class target is strictly defined across code and evaluation as: Short (0-20d, 31.95%), Medium (21-50d, 48.48%), and Long (>50d, 19.56%). Text references that casually stated '>40d' have been corrected to '>50d' to eliminate discrepancy with the majority baseline (48.48%) and the Long class frequency (19.56%).

clustering_quality_metrics.interpretation: Silhouette scores of 0.067 - 0.078 and Davies-Bouldin scores > 3.0 demonstrate that patient records form weakly separated groups with high internal dispersion and significant overlap, rather than cleanly isolated clusters.

cluster_profiles_verified.stay_differences_note: Differences between cluster mean stays are under 3 days (Cluster A: 33.58d, Cluster B: 31.66d, Cluster C: 30.68d; spread is 2.90 days).

outlier_ablation_verified.finding: Removing statistical outliers (Z > 3 on numeric fields, dropping 15,922 records) reduced accuracy by -0.50 percentage points (from 38.82% to 38.32%) and macro-F1 by -1.82 percentage points (from 0.1756 to 0.1574). In clinical healthcare data, high deposits and high visitor counts are valid signals of acute medical complexity, not measurement noise. Outliers were therefore retained.

ann_roc_auc.evaluation_provenance: Out-of-fold predicted probabilities across 5-fold GroupKFold(patientid) on 318,438 Kaggle hospital records (ANN MLPClassifier 64x32).

hierarchical_linkages.sampling_method: Uniform random subsample of N=15,000 patients (random_state=42) to satisfy O(N^2) memory constraints

summary_findings.chaining_effect_note: Single linkage suffers from extreme chaining (14,998 points in Cluster 0, 1 point in Cluster 1, 1 point in Cluster 2), yielding degenerate clusters despite high silhouette. Ward linkage produces the most balanced and compact clusters.
